# EnterpriseGlue v0.12.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.11.1`.

## Highlights

- **platform-administration:** Extends declarative configuration and bootstrap so operators can manage the complete supported platform-administration contract without an interactive administrator or Admin UI.

## User and administrator impact

- Platform administration can be supplied, previewed, applied, reconciled, and exported through the supported headless configuration workflow.
- Configuration-owned settings remain visible in the portal for diagnostics while interactive mutations are disabled or clearly identified as drift-prone.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Run database migration 1700000000110 before enabling the expanded headless administrative catalog.
- Existing interactive administration remains supported unless a deployment explicitly enables configuration ownership for the corresponding settings.
- Validate and preview the complete administrative bundle before enabling authoritative startup reconciliation in production.

## API and integration compatibility

- Extends the public configuration-bundle schemas, preview, diff, apply, export, and reconciliation receipts for complete supported administrative configuration coverage.

## Configuration

- Adds declarative coverage for the supported Platform Settings and administrative resource families that are not yet represented in EnterpriseGlueConfigBundle.
- Supports fail-closed startup bootstrap and reconciliation from a bounded local file while keeping credentials in approved secret references rather than bundle values.

## Database migrations

- Migration: 1700000000110 add portable Platform Settings section ownership, generic administrative-object ownership, and Environment Tag provenance.
- The migration is additive and preserves existing settings and Environment Tags as manually owned.
- TypeORM revert removes the new provenance tables and Environment Tag provenance columns; export and restore the owning bundle first because ownership history is not preserved by the downgrade.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Headless bootstrap is fail closed, validates exact bundle content and ownership, and never accepts literal credentials in configuration.
- Administrative changes retain audit, idempotency, tenant, authorization, endpoint-policy, and secret-resolution boundaries equivalent to the interactive APIs.
- SendGrid, Mailgun, and Mailjet credential delivery is restricted to exact built-in HTTPS provider hosts with production DNS pinning, redirect rejection, request timeouts, bounded responses, and sanitized public failures.

## Known limitations

- Runtime operational actions and user-specific workflows that are not durable platform configuration remain outside the declarative bundle contract.

## Rollback

- Restore the previous bundle and reapply it through the hash-bound configuration workflow before disabling authoritative bootstrap.
- Export the active bundle before database downgrade, disable bootstrap, revert migration 1700000000110, and redeploy the matching prior application images; do not edit configuration ownership directly in the database.

## Validation evidence

- Configuration schema, preview, diff, apply, export, idempotency, ownership, and rollback contract suites
- Fail-closed startup bootstrap, secret-reference, audit, tenant-boundary, and administrative API parity coverage
- Real PostgreSQL startup/restart/reapply coverage for persistence, secret resolution, machine-principal authentication and RBAC, export/no-op round-trip, mutation locks, and authoritative removal
- Real HTTP and CLI all-family lifecycle coverage plus a maintained browser workflow for locked, warning, and drifted ownership across administrator surfaces
- Backend and frontend typechecks, lint, authorization structure coverage, portable migration-up/down tests, and focused Admin API and portal tests
